A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VL-RouterBench and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained content can be matched reliably despite appendix additions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original router evaluations, encoder and fusion ablations, throughput measurements, and per-dataset results in Tables 2–4 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds metric-sensitivity, multi-cost, held-out-dataset, and routing-difficulty results in Appendix I.

M1.justification: Appendix I.3 extends the financial-cost objective and soft-label targets to incorporate KV-cache memory through a weighted, normalized multi-cost energy. This changes training targets for the extension while retaining the original routing architectures and single-cost procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 14 datasets across General, STEM, and Charts/OCR, with the same single-image tasks. The new held-out evaluation repartitions existing datasets rather than adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds a Random comparator in the routing-difficulty comparison in Figure A3. The comparator sets in the retained main and per-dataset experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds training on 11 datasets with MMMU, MathVision, and ChartQA held out, a beta sweep from 0.01 to 100, and KV-memory evaluation with Avg. Mem. and Tri-RankScore. Figure 5 also revises the reported E5-small-v2/BGE-M3 embedding dimensions from 1024/384 to 384/1024; this does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix I adds analyses of model complementarity across datasets, sensitivity to the Rank Score weight, generalization to held-out datasets, and accuracy stratified by the number of correct candidate models. These address substantially more diagnostic questions than v1's retained encoder, fusion, and backbone ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent trials and mean/standard-deviation reporting for the same main trainable-router experiments. The additions introduce no new run-count disclosure, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Tables A1–A2 and Figures A1–A3 add substantial results: RouterDC leads the multi-cost comparison, while VLC exceeds RouterDC on OOD Rank Score, 69.44 versus 68.88. Figure A2 shows Cheapest overtaking Oracle at beta 10 and 100. Table 3 changes Only-Text throughput from 147.21 to 350.96 and Only-Image from 1550.65 to 250.39. The original six appendix result tables remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix I.3 adds a two-cost optimization formulation, its generalized soft-label distribution, and a formal three-way weighted harmonic Tri-RankScore. These extend existing mathematics; the original soft-label proof and Pareto-fitting derivation remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the scientific claims about benchmark scope, cost-aware routing, competitive multimodal routers, and the remaining Oracle gap. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of complementary model strengths, beta as an application-dependent preference, and the Oracle gap as difficulty distinguishing among the few models capable of solving hard instances. It also limits the KV-memory proxy to accessible open-source architectures. The existing limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 documents constructing the KV-memory proxy from logged token counts and architectural parameters, with bounded log scaling. It changes a promised pipeline release to a reported pipeline/benchmark release, retaining the same repository link. Appendix H's optimizer, learning rate, batch size, and training budget remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 67 cited works and substantive related-work positioning are retained. Changes to citation back-references and typography do not alter the claimed relationship to prior routing benchmarks or methods.

P1.justification: There are limited grammar and notation edits, streamlined dataset/model descriptions, added author contact information and acknowledgments, and additional Appendix I subsections. The main narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: The appendix gains a model-accuracy heatmap, beta-sensitivity and routing-difficulty plots, and multi-cost and ID/OOD comparison tables, substantially expanding its visual analyses. Figure 5 is reformatted with revised dimension labels. The original appendix scatterplot and six result tables are retained as Figure A4 and Tables A3–A8.

improvement.justification: The added held-out evaluation, metric sensitivity, and difficulty analysis provide useful evidence about transferability and routing trade-offs that v1 lacked. The multi-cost extension also broadens practical evaluation. These gains are tempered by limited specification of the KV proxy and a new inconsistency: Appendix I.2 says Oracle always scores highest, whereas Figure A2 shows Cheapest ahead at beta 10 and 100.
